definitions.explanation: A literary word meaning to wind or meander. Almost exclusively encountered as part of the four-character compound {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ} (twists and turns, complications). Rarely used on its own in modern Japanese.

examples.japanese: {紆余|うよ}した{道|みち}を{歩|ある}く。
examples.english: To walk along a winding road.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}は{紆余|うよ}しながら{海|うみ}へ{向|む}かう。
examples.english: The river winds its way toward the sea.

examples.japanese: {紆余|うよ}を{経|へ}て、ようやく{結論|けつろん}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: After many twists and turns, we finally reached a conclusion.

notes:
A highly literary word that is almost always encountered as part of the four-character compound {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ} (twists and turns, complications). On its own, {紆余|うよ} means to wind or meander, both literally (of roads and rivers) and figuratively (of processes and events).

The characters break down as {紆|う} (to wind, to coil) + {余|よ} (to extend, to spread). Both characters suggest gradual, winding extension.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}: twists and turns, complications — by far the most common form
- {紆余|うよ}した{道|みち}: a winding road (literary)
- {紆余|うよ}を{経|へ}て: after going through twists and turns

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}: twists and turns — the standard four-character compound
- {曲折|きょくせつ}: bending, complications — can be used independently unlike {紆余|うよ}
- {蛇行|だこう}: meandering, winding — specifically for rivers or roads snaking back and forth
